resale_co.name: Residential Certificate of Inspection (formerly Certificate of Continued Occupancy, CCO)
resale_co.issued_by: Robbinsville Township Construction Office (Construction & Housing / Code Enforcement)
requirements: Smoke detectors on every level including the basement (not crawl spaces or unfinished attics); battery units must be 10-year sealed battery
Carbon monoxide detector no more than 10 feet outside the bedroom door (battery or electric)
No cracked window glass or broken window seals (cloudy panes)
Anti-tip bracket installed for the stove
No exposed wiring (uncovered junction boxes, switches, outlets, wire nuts)
Handrails on all stairways of four or more steps
Furnace flue sealed at the chimney
Pools need an enclosure with self-closing, self-latching gates that swing away from the pool
No garbage disposal under the kitchen sink when the home is on public sewer
Private well: Private Well Testing Act water test results
Septic: report on the State Onsite System Inspection Form by a licensed septic inspector
If the home will be rented, the owner must first register as a landlord with the Clerk's Office
resale_co.how_to_apply: Complete the Residential Certificate of Inspection request form and mail or drop it off at the Construction Office, 2300 Route 33, Robbinsville, NJ 08691, with a check or money order payable to Township of Robbinsville, credit card or exact cash. Inspections are scheduled Monday through Thursday between 3:30 pm and 6:00 pm only. Office hours 7:30 am to 3:30 pm.

evidence.quote: RESIDENTIAL & COMMERCIAL CERTIFICATES OF INSPECTION Formerly referred to as "Certificates of Continued Occupancy"
The following information is provided to assist property owners and realtors selling residential real estate property of certain requirements and common violations in CCO inspections.
The CCO inspection for each property may reveal additional violations that must be addressed, or other requirements that must be complied with, before a CCO can be issued by the Township.
Once a Certificate of Continued Occupancy is issued it is valid for 60 days.
Please complete the form which can be sent by mail or dropped off to the Construction Office with check, money order made payable to Township of Robbinsville, credit card or exact cash.
Please note that all inspections are scheduled Monday thru Thursday between 3:30pm & 6:00pm only.
Sandy DeLorenzo, Administrative Assistant (CCO Inspections/ Information) 2300 Route 33, Robbinsville, NJ 08691 609-259-3600 Ext. 1113 sdelorenzo@robbinsville.net
Roger Fort, Director of Construction & Housing/Code Enforcement Official 2300 Route 33, 3rd Floor, Robbinsville, NJ 08691 609-259-3600 Ext. 1105 rfort@robbinsville.net

resale_co.notes: The Township's own pages treat the residential Certificate of Inspection (CCO) as the resale certificate: the July 30, 2026 instructions are written for owners and realtors selling homes and ask for the closing date, but no ordinance text saying it is mandatory on every sale was found (ecode360 cannot be opened). The request form gives SandyD@robbinsville.net for questions; the Construction contact page lists sdelorenzo@robbinsville.net. Director of Inspections is Roger Fort (609-259-3600 Ext. 1105, rfort@robbinsville.net). The office checks for open permits and landlord registration when the request is filed. The request form header says 'CCI' (Certificate of Inspection) but the information sheet still uses 'CCO'.

requirements: Smoke/CO alarms are checked as 'State Mandated Requirements' in the Township CCO (Certificate of Inspection) inspection
Battery smoke detectors must be 10-year sealed battery type

authorities.name: Robbinsville Township Construction Office (smoke and CO checked in the Certificate of Inspection; the state directory lists the Construction Office for smoke detector compliance). The Robbinsville Township Fire Department Bureau of Fire Prevention is the fire code enforcing agency.
authorities.how_to_apply: Through the Construction Office residential Certificate of Inspection request (609-259-3600 Ext. 1113). No separate smoke/CO certificate form or fee was found on the Township site; the Fire Department website is behind a bot check.

fire_cert.notes: The July 2026 LEA registry lists the Robbinsville Township Fire Department (F) as the fire code enforcing agency; its Fire Official is Brian F Johnson, (609) 259-7814, bjohnson@robbinsville.net (state directory). The directory's smoke detector compliance entry is 'RobbinsvilleTwp Constr Office', phone (609) 259-7082; the Township site gives the Construction Office as 609-259-3600. The Fire Department's own site (robbinsvillefire.org) shows a bot check and was not opened; its archived fee schedule (Township Code 109-10, downloaded 2023) has no smoke certificate fee. No separate smoke/CO fee was found, so the $100 CCO fee appears to cover the alarm check. The Township's 'Smoke Detector Code Regulations' sheet (October 2025) quotes N.J.A.C. 5:70-4.19 and does not mention a fire extinguisher. The LEA registry notes Allentown Borough is in a shared service with Robbinsville (does not change Robbinsville).

other_items.label: Open permits and landlord registration
other_items.detail: The request form's office section checks 'Registered as landlord?' and 'Open permits?'. If the home will be rented, the owner must register as a landlord with the Clerk's Office before an inspection is scheduled.

other_items.label: Private well and septic
other_items.detail: Homes with a private well must provide Private Well Testing Act results; homes with septic must provide a septic report on the State Onsite System Inspection Form by a licensed septic inspector.

open_questions: Confirm the residential Certificate of Inspection is mandatory on every 1-2 family sale (no ordinance text was found) and how far before closing to apply.

Confirm whether the Fire Department issues any separate smoke/CO certificate or fee for 1-2 family sales, or whether the Construction Office CCO covers it; and whether an extinguisher or secondary power source label is checked.
